added_models.model: Mice injected with human IL-17A, plasma KC (CXCL1) readout

engagement.confidence_note: Report date of bTDR08 not given; year is the IND opening (2007-11-01) as proxy.
engagement.note: Human IL-17A injected into C57BL/6 mice raises plasma KC (mouse CXCL1); ixekizumab blocked it (sponsor report bTDR08), the filed in-vivo engagement test.
engagement.short: Ixekizumab blocks hIL-17A-induced KC in mice
engagement.quote: Ixekizumab administration decreased hIL-17 induced KC secretion in C57BL/6NHsd mice (Report bTDR08).
engagement.judgement: Opened at the IND date as the proxy for first use, as the draft does for the other filed ixekizumab studies. Izokibep was later run in the same challenge model (Klint 2023).

engagement.magnitude_basis: mouse plasma KC after hIL-17A challenge vs lesional CXCL1 mRNA in patients
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read via PMC (PMC3470466). Phase 1 NCT number not given in the paper; registry_date not found.
engagement.note: In ixekizumab-dosed patients' lesions CXCL1 and IL-8, the human homologues of the mouse KC readout, fell more than 6-fold by week 2.
engagement.quote: As illustrated in Figure 3, genes that were strongly suppressed (change >6-fold) by ixekizumab included: IL-19, a potent inducer of epidermal hyperplasia; IL-8 and CXCL1, known IL-17 induced chemokines with potent ability to attract neutrophils
engagement.reason: CXCL1 fell in patients as in mice
engagement.judgement: A pairing: the mouse result became public only in the 2015 FDA review (posted 2016), so the entry is dated 2016. Mouse readout is induced plasma KC; human readout is lesional CXCL1 mRNA, the same chemokine but a different compartment and no exogenous challenge, so downstream, not direct.

efficacy.confidence_note: Exact date of the mouse study not given; year is the first-in-human start (NCT02690142, 2016-02) as proxy, since the paper places it in preclinical development.
efficacy.note: Izokibep was run in the same hIL-17A/KC mouse model before first-in-human dosing (2016) and called 30- to 50-fold more effective than the antibodies.
efficacy.short: Mouse KC model: izokibep beats mAbs
efficacy.quote: On an mg/kg basis, izokibep provided 30- and 50-fold superior efficacy in reducing KC secretion relative to ixekizumab and secukinumab, respectively.
efficacy.judgement: The paper calls its in-vitro and in-vivo work 'preclinical psoriasis models' and claims superior efficacy, so the model made a psoriasis efficacy prediction for izokibep, which ixekizumab's filing did not.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Model side read in full (PMC10187109).
efficacy.note: Izokibep Phase 2 met its primary endpoint, PASI 90 at week 12: 71% on 80 mg vs 0% placebo. The predicted edge over ixekizumab was not tested head to head.
efficacy.quote: At week 12, PASI 90 response rates were 0%, 5%, 19%, 71% and 59% for the placebo, 2-, 20-, 80- and 160-mg izokibep groups, respectively.
efficacy.judgement: Scored on direction (izokibep works in psoriasis). The model's magnitude claim, 30-fold better than ixekizumab, has no head-to-head test; across trials izokibep's 71% PASI 90 is close to ixekizumab's Phase 3 rates, so the superiority looks over-stated, but that is my cross-trial reading and not scored. AFFIRM-35 (NCT03591887) has no registry results.

added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology of izokibep (only cross-reactive species)

dose.confidence_note: Year is the EudraCT registration (2015-004531-13) as proxy for the toxicology programme; the 26-week study may have completed later.
dose.note: Izokibep binds monkey but not rodent IL-17A; 26-week monkey NOAEL 20 mg/kg/week (human equivalent 6.5 mg/kg, 520 mg), limited by an injection-site abscess at 40.
dose.quote: due to the formation of local abscess and systemic sequelae that were considered as adverse event (AE) in one female administered 40 mg/kg/week, the NOAEL was determined to be 20 mg/kg/week
dose.judgement: A separate track from the draft's cyno-tox-ixekizumab because dose is split by modality and this is the protein (Affibody) member's own study.

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey NOAEL 20 mg/kg/week (HED 6.5 mg/kg) vs highest Phase 2 dose 160 mg q2w
dose.note: Patients took up to 160 mg every 2 weeks (about 1 mg/kg/week, under the 6.5 mg/kg human-equivalent NOAEL); harms matched placebo apart from mild injection-site reactions.
dose.short: Margin held at the effective dose
dose.quote: During the placebo-controlled period, AEs in the izokibep groups were similar to placebo except for mild injection site reactions.
dose.judgement: Paired by me: the effective dose (80-160 mg every 2 weeks, Phase 2) sits about 6-fold under the monkey NOAEL's human equivalent per week. The monkey's limiting harm was an injection-site abscess; patients had only mild injection-site reactions, so no toxicity block. AFFIRM-35 (NCT03591887) has no registry results.

considered_not_added: Surrogate anti-mouse IL-17 antibodies in collagen-induced arthritis and EAE mice (filed for ixekizumab): arthritis/MS models, no psoriasis prediction compared with psoriasis patients.
HT-29 GRO-alpha and dermal-fibroblast neutralisation assays (ixekizumab, izokibep IC50s): in-vitro potency only; no comparison with patient outcomes or exposures.

Ixekizumab population PK / exposure-response model used to set Phase 3 regimens (FDA ClinPharmR): fitted on the Phase 1/2 patients themselves, not an independent model system, and the review states no prediction-vs-Phase 3 comparison.

Secukinumab-based PK-PD model used to anticipate izokibep's 2 mg starting dose would give an 'incomplete and transient' effect (Klint 2023): sibling-drug in-silico model whose prediction is too vague to score (2 mg gave PASI 50 in 3/5 after one IV dose; 5% PASI 90 in Phase 2).

Imiquimod mouse and human-skin xenograft models: no study found comparing them with patient results for ixekizumab, izokibep, netakimab or vunakizumab (comparisons exist for secukinumab/brodalumab, outside the member list).
Netakimab and vunakizumab preclinical models: no preclinical or translational paper found in Europe PMC.
Patient-level response predictors (serum uric acid, blood biomarkers for ixekizumab): observational patient cohorts, not a model system.
Human genetics / Mendelian randomization for IL17A in psoriasis efficacy: none found; the inborn-errors safety track is already in the draft.
